title: Compare Aviva-reported actions (e.g., startup) against WCS/OptiSweep backend state to identify communication vs backend issues
summary: When Aviva shows an action such as “startup” but WCS/OptiSweep does not show the corresponding backend state, treat it as a communication issue and capture enough evidence to support later diagnosis.
when_to_use: Use when an Aviva-triggered action (example: “startup”) is reported as having been issued, but the backend system state in WCS/OptiSweep does not reflect that action.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Verify backend state visibility in WCS/OptiSweep for the specific action reported from Aviva, compare it to what Aviva indicates, and record the mismatch as evidence for communication-vs-backend diagnosis.
access_or_tools_needed: Ability to observe whether the backend state includes the reported action (example: “startup”)

visual_references.description: Training frame containing the diagnostic logic: compare Aviva-reported “startup” vs WCS/OptiSweep state; mismatch implies communication issue.

steps.title: Identify the Aviva-reported action to validate in the backend
steps.purpose: Establish the exact action label that Aviva indicates so you can check for the corresponding backend state.
steps.instruction: From the incident call/issue description, note the specific Aviva action that was reportedly triggered (example given: “startup”).
steps.expected_result: You have a specific action label from Aviva (e.g., “startup”) that you will look for in WCS/OptiSweep backend state.
steps.healthy_condition: The reported action is unambiguous (e.g., the caller can state “startup” as the action they clicked/triggered).
steps.failure_condition: The reported action is unclear or multiple actions are claimed without a specific label to validate.

actions.label: Record Aviva action label
actions.exact_action: Identify the action reportedly issued from Aviva (example given by the source: 'startup').

steps.title: Check WCS or OptiSweep backend state for the reported action
steps.purpose: Determine whether the backend system actually entered the state corresponding to the Aviva-reported action.
steps.instruction: Use WCS or OptiSweep state visibility to check whether the backend state includes the reported action (example: confirm whether “startup” appears in the backend state).
steps.expected_result: You can determine whether the backend state shows the reported action (e.g., whether “startup” is present in WCS/OptiSweep state).
steps.healthy_condition: The backend state reflects the reported action (e.g., backend shows “startup” when Aviva indicates “startup”).
steps.failure_condition: The backend state does not show the reported action (e.g., Aviva shows “startup” but WCS/OptiSweep shows no “startup”).

actions.label: Verify backend state
actions.exact_action: Check WCS or in our Opti sweep what is the state of the system.

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot access WCS/OptiSweep state visibility to perform the backend state check, escalate to a role with access to perform the backend state check.

steps.title: Compare Aviva indication vs WCS/OptiSweep backend state and classify the mismatch
steps.purpose: Convert the observed mismatch into the source-supported conclusion (communication issue vs backend state reflection).
steps.instruction: Compare what Aviva indicates (e.g., “startup”) against what WCS/OptiSweep shows. If Aviva put it in “startup” but you do not see “startup” in WCS/OptiSweep, classify it as a communication issue.
steps.expected_result: A clear conclusion is recorded: either backend reflects the action, or Aviva/backend mismatch is treated as a communication issue (example: Aviva shows “startup” but backend shows no “startup”).
steps.healthy_condition: Aviva and backend state match for the action label you validated.
steps.failure_condition: Aviva and backend state do not match for the action label (example explicitly supported: “startup” shown in Aviva but not in WCS/OptiSweep).

actions.label: Classify mismatch
actions.exact_action: If Aviva put it in startup, but we didn't, we don't see any startup, it's a communication issue.

steps.title: Record evidence of the Aviva/backend mismatch for later diagnosis
steps.purpose: Ensure the mismatch is captured as actionable evidence without over-claiming root cause beyond what the source supports.
steps.instruction: Document the observed mismatch between Aviva and WCS/OptiSweep (example: Aviva shows “startup” but WCS/OptiSweep shows no “startup”). Include enough notes to support later diagnosis.
steps.expected_result: A written note exists describing the specific action label and the observed backend state result (match vs mismatch), with the mismatch explicitly captured as evidence of a communication issue.
steps.healthy_condition: Your notes clearly state the Aviva action label and the backend state observation (e.g., “startup” missing in WCS/OptiSweep).
steps.failure_condition: Notes are vague (e.g., “something didn’t work”) and do not include the action label and the backend state observation.

actions.label: Capture mismatch evidence
actions.exact_action: Record this mismatch as evidence of a communication issue.

success_criteria: You determine whether the backend state in WCS/OptiSweep reflects the Aviva-reported action label (example: “startup”).
If there is a mismatch (Aviva shows “startup” but backend shows no “startup”), you classify it as a communication issue and record the mismatch evidence.
healthy_conditions: Backend state shows the same action label that Aviva indicates (no mismatch).
failure_conditions: Aviva indicates an action (example: “startup”) but WCS/OptiSweep does not show that action label (explicitly supported as a communication issue).
You cannot access WCS/OptiSweep state visibility to perform the backend state check.
escalation_guidance: If you cannot access WCS/OptiSweep state visibility to perform the backend state check, escalate to a role with access to perform the backend state check.
